newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai shares fall sharply at noon on bank sales.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai shares fall sharply at noon on bank sales.

text.p: Shanghai shares were sharply down at midday on Wednesday mainly due to state banks offsetting their positions in the market, traders said.
The domestic A share index lost 50.867 points or 3.93 percent to 1,245.038 points and the foreign currency B share index shed 2.012 points or 2.36 percent to 83.309 points.

"Banks have begun to offset their positions on a large scale in the past few trading days on the A share market," one trader said. "They sold particularly heavily this morning, which made the A share index fall sharply."
Traders said retail investors followed the banks to sell, making share prices fall even more quickly.
Sentiment on the B share market was hit by the sharp losses on the A share market, traders said.
Brokers said persistent rumours that Beijing would take further measures to cool down stock trading also contributed to this morning's falls.

A commentary by the official Financial Times based in Beijing said the central government would continue to take measures to cool down stock trading and would not support the stock markets because of China's takeover of Hong Kong in July.

"The commentary has made investors firmly believe the current market rumours will be confirmed eventually," said a second trader. "The indices are likely to move in negative territory for the rest of the session today."
Traders said the rumours included one saying that Beijing would shortly announce a three-day settlement system to replace the current one-day settlement system on the A share market.
By midday on Wendesday, a total of 6.9 million B shares valued at $4.5 million had been traded. On the A market, volume was 164.9 million shares worth 2.3 billion yuan.

Shanghai Steel Tube Co was the worst B share performer, losing $0.014 or 9.72 percent to $0.13 on volume of 60,000. Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co was the most actively traded on volume of 1.1 million shares, falling $0.030 or 2.13 percent to $1.138.
Sichuan Golden Summit Co was the worst A share performer, losing 0.70 yuan or 7.14 percent to 9.10 yuan on volume of 668,315 shares.
